answer: Yes, a meteg is printed. Host letter: ayin (ע), the only occurrence in the word. Host vowel: tsere.
visible_evidence: The whole word לעלא and all its lower points are visible and clear of the line below. From right to left under the word: the first lamed has a vertical two-dot sheva (:). The ayin has a horizontal two-dot tsere (..). Just left of the tsere, still under the left part of the ayin, is a separate short vertical stroke: the meteg. Under the second lamed is a qamats (a cross shape, separate from that stroke). Nothing is under the alef. The stroke cannot be a vowel stem, because tsere has no stem and the qamats is a separate mark further left. It is a single solid stroke, not sheva dots, and it is not ink from the next line, which starts well below. Per component: meteg present (high), host ayin (high), host vowel tsere (high).
